name: Creator Brand Partnership Media Kit
description: A warm editorial creator media kit that connects positioning, verified audience data, representative work, collaboration formats, case-study results, packages, rights, process, and contact.
style_guide:
# Creator Brand Partnership Media Kit

## Design intent

Create a working sales portfolio for an independent creator, influencer, expert, or small creator studio seeking thoughtful brand collaborations. The visual language is warm, direct, and editorial: soft cream paper, black evidence panels, coral-orange emphasis, tactile lifestyle photography, bold sans-serif type, candid italics, device-framed work examples, and visible proof behind audience and campaign claims.

The deck should answer who the creator is, who the work serves, what the audience evidence says, how the content feels, what partnership formats are available, what past work achieved, what packages cost, and how a project moves from intro to report. The reference previews are visual-language examples only. Do not copy their creator, portrait, handle, agency, positioning, content pillars, audience data, posts, client names, results, rates, packages, process, or contacts.

## Canvas and grid

- Use a fixed `1280 × 720 px` 16:9 canvas with `56–66 px` side margins, a `28–36 px` section header, and a `22–28 px` footer for handle, edition, rights, or validity.
- Use a 12-column grid with `16–20 px` gutters. Align portrait crops, positioning cards, audience strips, platform bars, work examples, style panels, format tables, case studies, package columns, process steps, and contact blocks.
- Reserve `100–132 px` for section label, direct headline, and one explanatory sentence. Keep each page focused on one partnership question.
- Prefer balanced `6/6` cover splits, three-pillar positioning rows, full-width proof strips, three-work examples, `6/6` format-and-case splits, and three-package comparisons.
- Use `18–24 px` between major modules and `10–14 px` within cards. Give images and proof points room; do not pack every post or brand into the deck.
- Most pages should remain warm and light. Use black panels for the one-line pitch, signature style, selected proof, recommended package, and other high-authority content.

## Color system

### Core palette

- Creator cream: `#F4EEE4`. Use for the main canvas and spacious editorial ground.
- Paper white: `#FFFDFC`. Use for cards, package fields, audience details, and clean device screens.
- Proof black: `#1A1715`. Use for primary typography, evidence strips, signature-style panels, selected cases, and premium packages.
- Action coral: `#FF6248`. Use for key phrases, section numbers, links, rates, calls to action, and selected performance deltas.
- Warm clay: `#B97555`. Use for lifestyle image harmony, secondary surfaces, and grounded visual warmth.
- Oat beige: `#DED3C3`. Use for quiet package columns, partner-fit panels, and process fields.
- Muted sage: `#7C826D`. Use sparingly for verified improvement, wellness or home-category context, and secondary content cues.
- Warm gray: `#817A72`. Use for notes, platform context, validity, and sources.

### Semantic use

- Coral means attention, creator voice, or an action to take; it does not automatically mean positive performance.
- Black panels signal evidence, recommendation, or a decisive statement and should remain scarce.
- Sage may indicate an approved or verified favorable state but should not become a second brand accent.
- Preserve accurate product, skin, interior, and food color in partnership imagery. Do not recolor sponsored work until the brand is misrepresented.

## Typography

- Use `Inter`, `Aptos`, `Helvetica Neue`, or another approachable editorial sans-serif.
- Use a restrained italic cut for the creator name, personal voice, one phrase in a headline, or a short testimonial. Avoid script fonts and generic influencer lettering.
- Cover title: `52–66 px`, regular to bold. Page headline: `32–42 px`, regular to medium. Section label: `9–11 px`, uppercase, tracked. Body: `14–17 px`. Metrics and format tables: `10–13 px`. Footers and terms: `8–10 px`.
- Use tabular numerals for followers, reach, engagement, subscribers, rates, views, clicks, sales, code uses, ROAS, timelines, and package totals.
- Keep the creator voice conversational, but keep commercial labels exact and scannable.

## Components

- Cards are flat white, cream, oat, coral, or black rectangles with thin borders, small corners, and no shadow.
- Positioning pillars need topic, audience need, share of content only when measured, and representative formats.
- Partner-fit modules should include aligned categories, values, production style, disclosure comfort, exclusions, and conflicts.
- Metric strips show platform, metric definition, period, source, and comparison basis.
- Device frames may display representative work but must not obscure post labels, platform, format, date, sponsorship status, or results.
- Partnership-format rows include deliverable, duration or count, creative approach, revision limit, rights, exclusivity, lead time, reporting, and rate basis.
- Package columns should remain directly comparable and highlight one recommended route only when appropriate.

## Charts and diagrams

- Favor platform performance bars, audience-profile cards, interest chips, representative-work grids, device mockups, signature-style specifications, format tables, case-study cards, package comparisons, and step-by-step project processes.
- Platform metrics must retain their native definitions. Do not compare view, reach, impression, follower, subscriber, and engagement values as if they were the same.
- Case studies should show objective, deliverables, organic or paid status, measurement window, source, outcome, benchmark, and the creator's role.
- Rate cards need to identify production, posting, licensing, whitelisting, paid media, exclusivity, travel, props, talent, revisions, tax, and rush fees as applicable.
- Process diagrams should show intro, brief, proposal, contract, production, review, disclosure, publish, report, and payment with realistic lead times.
- Avoid 3D charts, decorative follower counters, unsupported conversion funnels, and engagement gauges without definitions.

## Composition families

### Creator partnership cover

Split the canvas between a cream title field and one strong rights-cleared creator portrait or representative working image. Keep creator, representative, edition, rate validity, and a short positioning line visible.

### Positioning and partner fit

Use one black one-line pitch panel, three content pillars, and a clear partner-fit and exclusion panel. Make boundaries as visible as attractive categories.

### Platform metrics and audience

Use a black proof strip for headline metrics, platform bars for where the audience lives, and a white audience profile card with source, period, and demographic limits.

### Selected work and signature style

Show three representative pieces across distinct formats, each with platform, format, role, sponsorship status, and reason for inclusion. Add a black style panel defining palette, light, voice, music, editing, and clear avoidances.

### Partnership formats and case studies

Pair a concise format and rate table with recent case studies. Show comparable evidence without attributing all brand results to the creator.

### Packages, process, and contact

Use three starting packages, a clear five-step workflow, rights and reporting terms, rate validity, response expectation, and one direct contact route.

## Imagery

- Use rights-cleared creator portraits, real home or studio context, product use, food, wellness, interiors, travel, behind-the-scenes production, and representative published work.
- Preserve natural light, realistic skin and product color, lived-in texture, and the creator's actual visual signature.
- Keep device frames consistent and label posts accurately. Use direct exports or approved screenshots rather than reconstructed fake engagement UI.
- Obtain permission for brand assets, campaign imagery, comments, testimonials, collaborators, and recognizable private locations.
- Avoid generic influencer stock photos, fake social interfaces, purchased engagement screenshots, unlicensed brand logos, excessive ring-light imagery, over-retouched skin, and AI images presented as real partnerships.

## Content integrity

- Do not invent followers, reach, impressions, views, engagement, subscribers, audience demographics, interests, income, platform split, testimonials, partners, deliverables, results, rates, bookings, availability, or response times.
- State source, period, time zone, geography, platform, organic or paid distribution, aggregation method, and whether results are average, median, total, estimated, or guaranteed.
- Define engagement formula and denominator. Separate organic reach, boosted distribution, whitelisted ads, brand reposts, and cross-platform totals.
- Case studies must distinguish creator contribution from media spend, brand conversion systems, seasonality, offer, attribution, and other campaign factors.
- Clearly state disclosure, claims approval, usage rights, term, territory, paid amplification, whitelisting, exclusivity, category conflicts, revisions, cancellation, payment, and reporting.
- Health, wellness, beauty, food, finance, sustainability, or performance claims require appropriate evidence and compliant language.
- If information is missing, omit it or label it `estimate`, `illustrative`, `proposed`, `subject to availability`, `organic only`, or `to be confirmed`. Never fabricate proof to complete the deck.

## Avoid

- Do not copy preview creator identity, portrait, handle, studio, content pillars, audience, work, brand names, metrics, cases, rates, packages, process, or contacts.
- Do not present followers as reach, reach as impressions, views as unique people, engagement as purchase intent, or code uses as total attributable sales.
- Do not imply a brand relationship, endorsement, exclusivity, or testimonial without permission.
- Do not hide usage rights, paid media, whitelisting, category conflicts, revisions, fees, or disclosure terms.
- Do not use coral on every border and value; reserve it for creator voice and action.
- Do not use glossy gradients, glass cards, heavy shadows, oversized rounded corners, fake social UI, 3D charts, or unreadable commercial notes.
- Do not let aesthetic lifestyle imagery substitute for audience quality, deliverables, process, rights, or measurable evidence.
